signal.summary: 这项研究围绕视觉—语言—动作模型展开，关注机器人如何把视觉观察和语言指令，持续转换成跨时间的动作，而不是只对当前画面做一次反应。

editorial.intro: 这项研究围绕视觉—语言—动作模型展开，关注机器人如何把视觉观察和语言指令，持续转换成跨时间的动作，而不是只对当前画面做一次反应。

editorial.watch_next: 继续核对实验是否覆盖真实机器人、长时任务和跨场景泛化。

evidence.excerpt: Teaching Robots to Listen and Think Harder Physical Intelligence (π) Home Research Join Us Teaching Robots to Listen and Think Harder Published February 26, 2025 Email research@physicalintelligence.company Lucy Shi, Brian Ichter, Michael Equi, Liyiming Ke, Karl Pertsch, Quan Vuong, James Tanner, Anna Walling, Haohuan Wang, Niccolo Fusai, Adrian Li-Bell, Danny Driess, Lachy Groom, Sergey Levine, Chelsea Finn Paper Loading… When was the last time you cooked a new dish? You look at the recipe, lay out the ingredients, and get to work. There is a little voice inside your head — "oh I forgot, I need to add the tomato." You think carefully through each step, periodically checking the recipe. Maybe your friend chimes in — "watch out, you'll burn it." Daniel Kahneman described two different ways that people solve problems, which he dubbed "System 1" and "System 2." System 1 feels instinctual and automatic; System 2 is deliberative and conscious. Cooking that new dish used System 2: that's the little voice you heard in your head. When you do something for the 100th time, that's System 1: it feels automatic and you hardly think about it.
